concepts.title: Asexual Reproduction Modes
concepts.definition: Asexual reproduction creates offspring from a single parent without gametes: bacteria and amoeba divide by fission, yeast buds, hydra fragments, spores spread by fungi like Rhizopus, and plants multiply through stems, roots and leaves in vegetative propagation.
concepts.key_idea: One parent, exact copies: fission, budding, spores and vegetative propagation cover the modes.
question_patterns: describe binary fission in amoeba with a diagram
how does budding occur in yeast - explain with the process
what is fragmentation - give an organism that reproduces this way
explain spore formation in Rhizopus with the conditions helping it
name the vegetative parts used to propagate the given plants
why do offspring of asexual reproduction look identical to the parent

solution_steps.explain: One parent only, no gametes involved.
Fission, budding, fragmentation, spore formation or vegetative propagation.
Genetically identical copies inherit the parent's exact characters.

concepts.title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
concepts.definition: Flowers carry the reproductive parts: the stamen's anther makes pollen with male gametes, the pistil's ovary holds ovules with female gametes; pollination delivers pollen to the stigma, the pollen tube carries the gamete to the ovule, fertilisation forms the zygote, and the ovule matures into the seed inside the fruit.
concepts.key_idea: Pollen to stigma to ovule: fertilisation turns a flower into fruit and seed.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc107.txt section 7.2 (sexual reproduction in flowering plants)
question_patterns: draw a labelled diagram of a flower showing its reproductive parts
define pollination and differentiate self and cross pollination
describe the process of fertilisation in a flower step by step
what changes occur in the flower after fertilisation - list them
differentiate the male and female gametes of a flower
why are petals and sepals called accessory parts - explain

solution_steps.explain: Stamen bears pollen; pistil carries the ovule.
Pollen germinates on the stigma and its tube reaches the ovule.
Zygote becomes embryo; ovule becomes seed; ovary becomes fruit.

concepts.title: Human Reproductive System and Reproductive Health
concepts.definition: In humans, the male system delivers sperm through testes and ducts, the female system prepares eggs, receives sperm and nurtures the embryo in the uterus; puberty brings body changes, and reproductive health needs awareness of contraception methods and safe practices against sexually transmitted diseases.
concepts.key_idea: Testes make sperm, ovaries make eggs, uterus nurtures - and health knowledge protects it all.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc107.txt sections 7.3 (human reproductive system, reproductive health)
question_patterns: draw and label the human male and female reproductive systems

solution_steps.explain: Male parts make and deliver sperm; female parts make eggs and nurture embryos.
Sperm meets egg; the zygote implants in the uterus and grows.
Contraception and safe practices guard reproductive health.
